extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, and patent examiners (Finnish national procedure, PRH)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting and responding to Finnish national patentability examination (PRH), including substantive patentability standards (software, biotech, medical methods, public_order) and procedural stages (formal/technical/approving communications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical character of computer-implemented inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an invention implemented by computer program corresponds to an implementation in logical circuits, and the circuit implementation is patentable (technical), then the same invention implemented by software is also patentable. (Finnish: "Jos loogisilla piireillä toteutettu keksintö on patentoitavissa eli se on luonteeltaan tekninen, on sama keksintö ohjelmalla toteutettuna myös patentoitavissa.")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice of implementation (hardware vs software) depends on economic/practical reasons. However, merely using conventional computing means does not guarantee patentability if the program executed on a computer causes only normal physical effects (e.g., current flow). You cannot make non‑patentable subject matter patentable by adding technical features that do not achieve technical effects beyond normal computing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical effect requirement for software
rubrics_metrics.description: A computer-implemented invention is patentable only if, when executed on a computer, it produces a technical effect that is more than what arises in normal data processing performed by any computer program. (Finnish: "Jos tietokoneohjelmalla toteutettu keksintö omaa teknisen luonteen, ts. se saa tietokoneessa suoritettuna aikaan teknisen vaikutuksen, joka on enemmän kuin mikä ilmenee tavanomaisessa tietojenkäsittelyssä...")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical effects include improvements in industrial process control, handling information representing physical quantities, control of computer or interface circuits, increased process efficiency or safety, faster operation or data transfer. If no such additional technical effect is achieved, patentability is not supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming computer programs and program products
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptable claim formulations include: method claims for a data-processing method implemented by a computer program; a computer program comprising code means arranged to perform all steps of method claims 1–N when executed; and a computer-readable storage medium storing such program code. (Finnish examples given for these claim types.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program/product claims are acceptable provided the underlying method or device claims (1–N) are themselves allowable. Program claims must define the special features necessary to achieve the intended technical effect and must not contain full program listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence principle for program and method/device claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle: a claim directed to the computer program or program product should define a technical effect similar to that obtained by a corresponding method- or device-claim executed on computing equipment. (Finnish: "Periaatteena on se, että tietokoneohjelmaa itseään ... koskevassa patenttivaatimuksessa keksintö määritellään siten, että tietokoneella suoritettuna saa aikaan samanlaisen teknisen vaikutuksen kuin... menetelmä- tai laitevaatimuksen mukaisella keksinnöllä.")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the scope of protection of the program claim cannot be determined merely by referring to method/device claims, the program claim must fully express the invention (see B.4.3.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: No patentability by adding only conventional technical means
rubrics_metrics.description: Adding technical limitations (e.g., known computing devices) to patent claims does not render non-patentable subject matter patentable if those limitations do not achieve technical effects beyond normal computer operation. (Finnish: "tavanomaisten tietojenkäsittelyvälineiden käyttö ei pelkästään riitä takaamaan patentoitavuutta...")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must assess whether claimed technical features produce more than routine physical effects (like electrical current) in order to support patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for claims in distributed systems
rubrics_metrics.description: For distributed systems, each unit/system may have corresponding method claims; the claim set must be unitary and satisfy novelty, inventive step and clarity for each unit. Interactions between units must be described so that all technical features appear from the claims. If method steps are performed in different units, it must be clear which unit performs which steps. (Finnish: "Eri yksiköiden väliset vuorovaikutukset tulee kuvata, jotta kaikki tekniset ominaispiirteet käyvät vaatimuksista ilmi... mitkä menetelmävaiheet kukin yksikkö suorittaa.")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity requires specification of per-unit responsibilities; refer to EPO guidance (EPO GL F-IV, 3.9.3) for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to resolve technical character under PatL 1 §
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claim does not on first view possess technical character, the question must be resolved under PatL 1 § before proceeding to novelty/inventive-step assessment. Otherwise, assess novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability as usual. (Finnish: "Jos patenttivaatimusten mukainen keksintö ei ensi näkemältä omaa teknistä luonnetta, tulee asia ratkaista PatL 1 §:n perusteella. Muussa tapauksessa tulee päätös keksinnön patentoitavuudesta tehdä... uutuuden, keksinnöllisyyden ja teollisen käyttökelpoisuuden arvioinnin perusteella.")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Software-related business-methods using known IT means may be non-technical; examiner should first decide exclusion under PatL 1 § (see E.6.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting computer-program claims — necessary features only
rubrics_metrics.description: In patent claims directed to computer programs, the invention must be defined by the particular features necessary to achieve the intended effect; claims must not include program listings. (Finnish: "Patenttivaatimuksessa keksintö on määriteltävä niiden erityispiirteiden avulla, jotka ovat välttämättömät tarkoitetun vaikutuksen aikaansaamiseksi. Vaatimukset eivät saa sisältää ohjelmalistausta.")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should focus on technical-functional features rather than literal code; program listings belong in the description if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptability of program claims when method/device claims lack clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: If program/device claims refer to method/device claims but the scope of protection is not unambiguously determinable by such reference, the program claim must fully disclose the invention in the claim language. (Finnish: "Jos hakemuksen menetelmä- tai laitevaatimukset ovat sellaiset, että haetun patenttisuojan laajuus ei käy yksiselitteisesti selville pelkästään viittaamalla niihin tietokoneohjelmaa koskevassa patenttivaatimuksessa, ... keksintö on ilmaistava patenttivaatimuksissa täydellisesti.")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particular attention where method/device claims include features not realizable by software.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of technical vs non-technical software effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of technical software implementations: industrial process control, processing information representing physical quantities, control of computer or its interface circuits. The effects may manifest as improved process efficiency/safety or faster computer operation/data transfer. (Finnish examples provided.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these examples to argue technical character in responses; mere data processing without physical/technical consequences is less likely to be patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surgical methods exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: PatL 1 §(3) excludes surgical methods directed to humans or animals from patentability. The surgical nature depends on the character of the method, not its purpose; if any step contains a surgical procedure the method is surgical. (Finnish: "Menetelmä katsotaan kirurgiseksi, jos sen yksikin vaihe sisältää kirurgisen toimenpiteen.")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment of surgical nature considers whether performance requires medical expertise, involves significant health risks, how complex and invasive it is. Minor procedures without special medical skill and small risks (tattooing, piercing, microdermabrasion, laser hair removal) may be patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Therapeutic methods exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Therapeutic methods (curing or preventing disease or correcting malfunction) directed to humans or animals are excluded: a method is therapeutic if any step includes a therapeutic intervention. (Finnish: "Menetelmä katsotaan terapeuttiseksi, jos menetelmän yksikin vaihe sisältää ihmiseen tai eläimeen kohdistuvan terapeuttisen toimenpiteen.")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-therapeutic treatments directed to animals/humans (e.g., methods to improve growth in sheep) can be patentable. Methods concerning operation of a therapeutic device can be patentable if there is no functional link between the method and the device's therapeutic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods on removed tissues/fluids
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for handling tissues or fluids removed from the body are patentable if the tissues/fluids are not returned to the same body. (Finnish: "Kehosta poistettujen kudosten tai nesteiden käsittelymenetelmä on patentoitavissa, jos kudoksia tai nesteitä ei palauteta samaan kehoon.")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: blood processing for storage (blood bank) can be patentable; dialysis, where blood is returned to the same body, is not patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic methods exclusion and definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A diagnostic method comprises four main phases: (1) examination/data collection, (2) comparison of data to standards, (3) finding a significant deviation/symptom, and (4) reasoning to associate deviation with a clinical picture (diagnosis). A diagnostic method is excluded under PatL 1 §(3) only if the examination phase requires presence of the tested human or animal. (Finnish: list of four phases and exclusion condition.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In vitro diagnostic methods (e.g., blood/urine analysis) are patentable. If a diagnostic claim lacks one of these phases, examiner may request inclusion to meet PatL 8 §(2) sufficiency/precision requirements. Methods producing only measurement data that do not enable treatment decisions may be patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of technical aids in diagnostic methods
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing whether a method is diagnostic, it is not decisive whether technical aids are used in the method phases; preparatory steps like adjusting equipment for an assay are not considered part of the examination phase. (Finnish: "Arvioitaessa menetelmän diagnostista luonnetta... ei ole merkitystä, sisältääkö menetelmävaatimus edellä esitettyjen vaiheiden menetelmävaiheissa teknisiä apuvälineitä.")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on whether the research phase requires presence of a human/animal. In vitro methods that do not require presence are patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant varieties, animal breeds and essentially biological methods exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant varieties, animal breeds and essentially biological breeding methods are not patentable (PatL 1 § 4 and 5). This includes genetically modified variety/ breed. However, a plant/animal can be subject-matter of an invention if it is not limited to a specific variety or breed. Technical methods for breeding are patentable, but methods that are essentially biological (contain steps based on natural phenomena like crossing or selection) are excluded. (Finnish: summary of PatL 1 § 4 and 5.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative protection (UPOV) exists for plant varieties. Refer to EPO decisions (G 2/07 etc.) for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public order and morality exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Any invention whose commercial exploitation is contrary to public order or good morals is excluded from patentability (PatL 1 b §). This is intended to prevent protection for inventions leading to criminal or generally offensive behaviour. (Finnish: summary.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illegality alone does not automatically make commercial exploitation contrary to public order; inventions with both acceptable and unacceptable uses should not include specific reference to the unlawful use in the application (example: method to open locked safes). Biotech moral exclusions are listed in PatL 1a and 1b and include human body in various stages, mere discoveries of human body substances, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to cite legal basis in examiner communications
rubrics_metrics.description: When PRH takes a position in an intermediate decision or other correspondence on patentability, it must indicate which statutory provision the position, request or decision is based on. (Finnish: "Hallintolain mukaan viranomaisen on esitettävä perustelut päätökselleen... kun PRH ottaa välipäätöksessä tai muussa kirjeenvaihdossa kantaa keksinnön patentoitavuuteen, se samalla ilmoittaa, mihin säädöskohtaan kannanotto... perustuu.")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All substantive objections should reference PatL, PatA or PatM provisions as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stages/types of PRH communications
rubrics_metrics.description: PRH uses several document types during examination: formal notice (muodollinen välipäätös), technical notice (tekninen välipäätös), and approving (acceptance) notice (hyväksyvä välipäätös). Each has defined purposes and timing. (Finnish: list of three types.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal notices concern formal defects; technical notices concern substantive patentability issues; approving notices indicate intention to grant subject to formalities and applicant confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal notice triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: PRH may issue a formal notice at various phases for formal defects such as insufficient clarity/precision of the invention (B.4.1), defects in abstract or figures, additional fee request when claim count exceeds paid number, or to request other offices' search results (PatL 74 § 3 mom.). (Finnish: examples given.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal notices may be replaced by informal phone contact for minor issues. If applicant has amended to claim subject-matter not apparent at filing (PatL 13 § / PatA 19 §), PRH may object by formal notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and content of the first technical notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The first technical notice's main purpose is to give the applicant a clear picture of the patentability of the invention so they can decide whether to continue prosecution in Finland and abroad. It describes the subject of the novelty search, the basis for the search, and for each examined claim addresses novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability. (Finnish: description of first technical notice.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice should justify any limitations on the search and list prior art cited in novelty assessment. It should explain reasons for lack of inventive step typically using the problem-solution approach (E.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty search scope and citation of unpublished earlier national applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty assessment takes into account earlier patent and utility model applications not yet public if they are likely to become public and will have legal effect in Finland. If such earlier applications are national and not public at time of notice, their identifying data and content are not disclosed in the notice; only that such an earlier application exists. (Finnish: explanation.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an earlier PCT publication's relevance to Finland is uncertain at the time of the notice, PRH may only mention it and address it in a later notice if it is found to concern Finland.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step assessment basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventive step (keksinnöllisyys) is assessed based on publications found in the novelty search and the skilled practitioner's knowledge and expertise; the problem-solution approach is used as described in E.4. (Finnish: "Olennaisen eron arvioinnin perustana ovat uutuustutkimuksessa esille tulleet tekniikan tason julkaisut... ja alan ammattilaisen muu tietämys ja ammattitaito.")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If judged not to differ significantly from known technique, PRH will justify refusal, normally using the problem-solution method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability requirement and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention must be industrially applicable (PatL 1 §) — i.e., it must work as intended. If operability is not credible, applicant is asked for further evidence. Patentability may be refused if invention appears not to function as intended. (Finnish: explanation.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may withhold novelty search until applicant proves operability in borderline cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of substantive defects leading to technical notice objections
rubrics_metrics.description: If PRH considers that the application has deficiencies affecting patentability, the technical notice will state the deficiencies with reasons. Examples: (•) claim concerns non-patentable subject-matter (PatL 1/1a/1b); (•) claim lacks novelty and/or inventive step (PatL 2 §); (•) claims are indefinite (PatL 8 §); (•) claims are not supported by the description enabling skilled person (PatL 8 §); (•) application lacks unity (PatL 10 §); (•) patent sought for subject-matter not apparent in original application (PatL 13 §). (Finnish: bullet list from text.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical notice should also explain which parts of the description/claims the novelty search covered and justify any limitations. It may also point out drafting or formatting issues (e.g., two-part claim form, translations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple technical notices policy
rubrics_metrics.description: A second technical notice is issued if new relevant publications appear after the first notice, if the invention is patentable but claims cannot be accepted in current form, or if the invention remains unpatentable and applicant's response raises issues requiring PRH reply. Further technical notices beyond the second are rare and issued only for newly arisen obstacles or significant claim amendments. (Finnish: description.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRH aims in the first technical notice to give clear instructions so fewer further notices are needed. New third+ notices only for new grounds or substantial claim changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approving (acceptance) notice conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: When the invention is patentable based on the examination and the application is acceptable as-is or with minor corrections, PRH issues an approving notice informing the applicant how the patent will be granted and requesting confirmation that the applicant wants a patent in that form. A prerequisite is that claims are acceptable in substance and wording. (Finnish: description of hyväksyvä välipäätös.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approving notice may request translations of claims and abstract and permit minor corrections; substantial formal defects are handled in a separate formal notice. If claims are amended after an approving notice (e.g., due to a third-party observation), a second approving notice may be issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions after PatL 19 § notice (no broadening/division)
rubrics_metrics.description: After PRH has given the PatL 19 § notice that the application can be accepted, claims may not be amended to broaden protection, nor may a new (divisional) application be created by splitting/parting the application (PatA 22 and 23 §§). The notice is given only when publishable documents are available. (Finnish: explanation.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to prevent changes that would unnecessarily prolong grant procedure. Applicants must pay publication fee within two months or the application lapses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possibility to delay grant (postponement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Granting of the patent may be postponed only if granting would occur before the application becomes public under PatL 22 § (i.e., within 18 months from filing/priority). Applicant can request postponement until 18 months from filing/priority. Applicant must make the request in writing and pay the publication fee within two months of the PatL 19 § notice for postponement to be accepted. (Finnish: F.6 summary.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If postponement accepted, certificate is sent after publication fee paid; applicant can also choose to delay grant to avoid earlier public disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to approve issuance and possible new obstacles
rubrics_metrics.description: PRH decides to accept the application unless a new obstacle appears after the PatL 19 § notice — e.g., a claim by a third party for better right, or a newly submitted prior art in a third-party observation showing lack of novelty or inventive step. Decision to accept is not made before 12 months from filing/priority so that later-published prior applications may be used in dispute. (Finnish: F.7 summary.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If acceptance is delayed because applicant asked for postponement or other conditions apply, PRH takes those into account; acceptance will be withheld until such periods expire.
